The *Niddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 25) is a verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* collection in the Pali canon. In the text, a female deity (*deva*) recounts her past merits and explains the rewards and benefits arising from unshakable faith in the Triple Gem.

 However, DharmaNexus records substantial Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 172 matching passages across 24 texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest reuse partner is the text's primary commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, alongside passages shared with the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* and *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares extensive formulaic verses and segments with other celestial mansion narratives in the *Vimānavatthu*—particularly the *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Soṇadinnāvimānavatthu* (Vv 23), *Bhadditthivimānavatthu* (Vv 22), *Uposathāvimānavatthu* (Vv 24), and *Suniddāvimānavatthu* (Vv 26)—as well as canonical discourses like the *Nimijātaka* (Ja 541) and the *Catumahārājasutta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3.37) [DharmaNexus].
